title: Encoder does not kill the first surviving clause
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables in which no term contains two distinct literals over the same variable, and let $w$ be a natural-number width parameter. Fix two restrictions $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ on the $n$ variables such that $\sigma$ leaves a variable free whenever $\rho_0$ does (that is, $\rho_0(v)$ undefined implies $\sigma(v)$ undefined), and let $t$ be the first term of $f$, in list order, that is not killed by $\rho_0$. Run the recursion at the heart of the Razborov encoding on $f$ and $w$ — with any fuel budget, any decision path, initial data $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$, and empty accumulated data — and write $\rho$ for the restriction it returns as its first component. Then for every literal $l$ of $t$ whose variable is left free by $\rho_0$, the output restriction $\rho$ does not kill $l$: it does not fix the variable of $l$ to the value that would make $l$ false.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a DNF formula on $n$ variables
no term of $f$ has two distinct literals on the same variable
arbitrary fuel budget, decision path, and empty accumulator for the encoding recursion
$\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ are restrictions on the $n$ variables
$t$ is the first term of $f$ not killed by $\rho_0$
caveat: The core function, the recursive worker of the Razborov encoding, is not among the supplied definitions, so its internal behaviour cannot be rendered faithfully; the prose describes it only as an opaque recursion returning a restriction. The remaining hypotheses and the conclusion (the returned restriction does not fix the free literal's variable to its falsifying value) are fully determined by the Lean statement.
replaced:
Let $f$ be a DNF whose terms contain no two distinct literals on the same variable, and
let $t$ be the first term of $f$ not killed by $\rho_0$ (as returned by
\texttt{find?}). If $l \in t$ has $\rho_0\,l.\mathrm{var} = \mathrm{none}$ and $\sigma$
is unset wherever $\rho_0$ is, then the first component of the encoder loop
\texttt{SwitchingLemma2.razborovEncode}'s \texttt{go} (for any fuel, path, and empty
accumulator) at $l.\mathrm{var}$ is not $\mathrm{some}\ l.\mathrm{neg}$; the encoder
never assigns the free literal $l$ its negating value, so it does not kill the first
surviving clause.
